title: U.S. House · Washington's 4th District
area: Central Washington, including the Tri-Cities (Kennewick, Pasco, Richland) and Yakima Valley.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Dan Newhouse (R) is listed by Ballotpedia among the district's "withdrawn or disqualified" 2026 primary candidates and did not appear on the August 4 primary ballot, leaving this an open-seat race. Amanda McKinney (R) led the top-two primary with 34.9% of the vote, followed by John Duresky (D) with 30.8%, out of eleven primary candidates including Jerrod Sessler and state Sen. Matt Boehnke.

candidates.name: Amanda McKinney
candidates.ballotNote: Led the August 4 top-two primary with 34.9% of the vote

summary.text: Amanda McKinney is a Republican member of the Yakima County Commission running in the open 4th District race. She has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has limited documented public statements.

background.text: Currently serves on the Yakima County Commission.

positions.summary: Says she will oppose gun control in Congress and has testified against gun restrictions as a county commissioner.
positions.quote: In Congress, Amanda will oppose unconstitutional gun control and stand firm in defense of the right of Americans to protect themselves, their families, and their communities.

positions.summary: Supports protecting Title IX and limiting women's sports to biological females, according to her campaign website.
positions.quote: She supports protecting Title IX and ensuring that women’s sports remain for biological females.

record.text: Serves as a Yakima County Commissioner.

candidates.name: John Duresky
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary with 30.8% of the vote

summary.text: John Duresky is a Democratic candidate and Air Force veteran running for the open 4th District seat, emphasizing affordability, healthcare access, and government accountability.

background.text: Describes himself as a veteran and a former federal civil servant with experience navigating VA and federal employment systems.
Campaign website describes him as a retired Air Force Major with three combat deployments.

priorities.text: Lists affordability and economic fairness as a top priority, citing rising grocery, housing, health-premium and tariff costs, and calls for restoring congressional authority over tariffs.

On healthcare, says he will work to keep rural hospitals open, restore ACA subsidies, and protect Medicare and Medicaid, while saying he believes the nation should eventually move toward universal healthcare.
On immigration, calls for secure borders paired with a pathway to legal status and citizenship, and says ICE "requires major structural reform" based on his experience as a former civil servant.

Campaign website says he supports removing the stepped-up basis and carried-interest tax loopholes, raising the federal minimum wage, and protecting federal employees from what he calls politically motivated mass firings.

positions.summary: Calls for closing the stepped-up basis and carried-interest tax loopholes, describing the tax code as favoring the wealthiest 1%.
Campaign issues page says he will fight to raise the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage so work actually pays

positions.summary: Says he will fight to remove tariffs that he says hurt farmers and raise consumer prices.
positions.quote: Remove harmful tariffs that hurt our farmers and raise prices for consumers

positions.summary: Supports restoring and expanding ACA subsidies, protecting Medicare and Medicaid from cuts, and moving toward universal healthcare access.
positions.quote: Restore and expand ACA subsidies to make insurance affordable

researchNotes: McKinney has not completed a Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website statement was found on her Ballotpedia page, so her positions and priorities could not be documented; researchDepth is minimal. Whether Rep. Dan Newhouse withdrew voluntarily or was excluded from the ballot was not independently confirmed beyond Ballotpedia's 'withdrawn or disqualified' listing.
